title: Do VLMs Share Safety Neurons Across Modalities?
abstract: arXiv:2608.30750v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can comply with harmful requests delivered through images, even when their LLM backbones would refuse the same content in text. While prior work characterizes these jailbreaks empirically or at the representation level, how visual inputs perturb safety pathways at the neuron level remains uncharted. We close this gap with a causal, neuron-level analysis of safety mechanisms in 10 VLMs. We propose a two-stage detection pipeline with iterative ablation that accounts for self-repair, and introduce two modality-isolated benchmarks, ViSafe-Detect and ViSafe-Eval, which decouple visual and textual safety signals.   Our analysis reveals: (i) Text safety in VLMs is localizable: $\sim$88 neurons ($<$0.01%) whose targeted ablation substantially reduces refusal. translated_title: 视觉语言模型是否跨模态共享安全神经元？
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）能够通过图像响应有害请求，即使其LLM骨干在文本形式下会拒绝同样的内容。尽管先前的工作从经验层面或表征层面刻画了这些越狱攻击，但视觉输入如何在神经元层面扰动安全通路仍属未知。我们通过对10个VLM进行因果性、神经元层面的分析来填补这一空白。我们提出了一个考虑自我修复现象、包含迭代消融的两阶段检测流程，并引入两个模态隔离的基准ViSafe-Detect和ViSafe-Eval，以解耦视觉和文本安全信号。我们的分析揭示：（i）VLM中的文本安全是可定位的：约88个神经元（占比<0.01%），针对性消融它们会大幅降低拒绝率。（ii）文本安全神经元构成主要的拒绝通路：消融它们是唯一能持续且显著降低拒绝率的干预手段。
tldr: 本文通过对10个VLM的因果性神经元级分析，发现文本安全由约88个神经元主导并构成主要拒绝通路，而视觉输入可在神经元层面绕过该安全机制，同时提出了考虑自我修复的检测流程和两个模态隔离基准ViSafe-Detect与ViSafe-Eval。
